subject: GRC partner onboarding: evidence workflow & pen-test coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Grant <sofia@securebridge.io>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auditlane.co>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GRC partner onboarding: evidence workflow & pen-test coordination

Hi Sofia / Liam —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Contoso wants a single integrated workflow to accept SOC2 evidence and coordinate a vendor-run pen test that can feed results into their GRC platform. We sketched a few possibilities during the call; attaching a first-pass scope and an evidence matrix to accelerate alignment.

High-level ask from Contoso:
- Centralized evidence ingest (S3/secure share + API) that maps to their control IDs.
- Pen test orchestration: vendor (AuditLane) to deliver findings into the GRC tool with attachments and risk tags.
- Minimal manual steps for their InfoSec team during the November audit window.

Proposed next steps (short, actionable):
1) SecureBridge (Sofia) to confirm API/connector requirements by EOD Thu.
2) AuditLane (Liam) to confirm expected artifact formats for pen test reports (JSON vs PDF + meta).
3) Redwood (Evelyn/Jonas) to propose a small integration PoC: a one-week run that wires the S3 evidence export -> SecureBridge ingest -> Contoso GRC mapping.

I've attached: Redwood_SecureBridge_Onboarding_Scope_v1.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-matrix.csv, PenTest-scope-draft.pdf

Ben
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--

From: Sofia Grant <sofia@securebridge.io>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: GRC partner onboarding: evidence workflow & pen-test coordination

Thanks Ben — good summary. Quick answers from SecureBridge side:
- Connector surface: we support S3 pulls + an authenticated REST ingest endpoint. Preferably we fetch zipped evidence bundles and parse metadata CSVs (your matrix looks ideal).
- Control mapping: we can accept a mapping CSV or a small mapping API (we support both).
- Audit trail: each evidence item is fingerprinted and stored with sha256 + timestamp; we'll preserve original files for 90 days (configurable for enterprise).

We reviewed the attached PoC scope and have two clarifying questions:
1) For the PoC, will Redwood host a test S3 (short-lived) or do you expect SecureBridge to host a temporary collection endpoint?
2) Pen-test artifacts: we can ingest JSON findings natively; PDFs will be attached as blobs and linked to the finding record. Is AuditLane planning to produce structured JSON?

We can confirm connector detail by Thursday. If that works, we suggest a kickoff call Fri morning to align roles.

—Sofia
Director, Integrations
SecureBridge

--

Hi all — quick note from AuditLane on formats and scheduling:
- Deliverables: final pen test report (PDF), separate findings export (JSON, array of findings) with standardized fields (id, title, severity, cvss, description, remediation, evidence_refs).
- Attachments: screenshots and packet captures will be provided as individual files with stable filenames and hashes.
- Timing: we have availability to run an external network + web app test during the week of Oct 18; internal infra testing could be scheduled in early Nov if Contoso approves.

For the PoC we can produce a mock JSON feed and a zipped PDF set. That should be enough to validate ingestion and mapping.

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Technical Delivery
AuditLane

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GRC partner onboarding: evidence workflow & pen-test coordination

Ben / team —

Thanks both (Sofia / Liam) for the quick feedback. Internal notes and a proposed tactical plan below.

Concise technical approach for PoC:
- Redwood will stand up a short-lived S3 bucket (redwood-contoso-poc-2026-07) and create signed URLs for SecureBridge to pull.
- AuditLane will upload a zipped package: findings.json + reports/ (pdfs + supporting files).
- Redwood will run an ingestion job that maps findings.json -> internal issue records and then POSTs to SecureBridge mapping API to create control links.

Minimum success criteria (PoC):
- SecureBridge successfully ingests the zipped bundle and maps to Contoso control IDs (matching at least 90% of sample mapping rows).
- AuditLane findings JSON parses without schema errors and attachments link to findings in SecureBridge.
- Contoso InfoSec can view the mapped evidence in their GRC workspace and export an audit-ready package.

Action items (owners + due):
- Ben: finalize commercial scope with Contoso (confirm PoC acceptance criteria) — due Thu EOD.
- Jonas: create S3 bucket + IAM creds for the PoC — due Thu 14:00 PDT.
- Evelyn: build a small ingestion script and a schema validator for findings.json — due Fri 12:00 PDT.
- Vanessa: coordinate Contoso schedule and secure approvals for external testing windows — due Fri EOD.

I'll assemble a one-page runbook and share by Fri morning.

Evelyn
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

All — quick status and confirmations from Contoso: they approved the PoC scope with one caveat — data residency. Contoso requires that the PoC artifact storage is located in us-west-2 (their compliance policy).

Ben — can Redwood ensure the temporary S3 is in us-west-2?
Sofia — SecureBridge noted their ingest service is multi-region but will need a us-west-2 endpoint for the prod rollout; for PoC a pull from us-west-2 is fine.
Liam — AuditLane: can you mirror test artifacts to an s3 bucket in us-west-2 for the Oct window?

If everyone confirms, I'll book the Fri kickoff (next week) and drop the runbook + calendar invite.

Vanessa Ortiz
